## Advance several blocks in one process (`distribute.blocks_per_process`) {#sec-ch01-mesh}

### Summary

A `Mesh` holds several blocks in one process. It clones the block options for each, gives each block its own piece of
the grid, and runs their stages through one stage executor shared by all the blocks and a small worker pool. On a
CUDA device every worker has its own stream. The mesh also does once what each block would otherwise do alone: the
time-step reduction, the redo decision and the stage's global phase (the axial-momentum closure and, on the last
stage, the chemistry step).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: clone and repartition the options, run the blocks' stages, the global phase, then exchange.

**Data.** In: one options tree and `blocks_per_process`[^rg-8de7fd51747b]. Out: the local blocks, each with its own variable map.

**Placement.** Once per stage: the blocks' stages, the global phase, then the exchange.

**Activation.** YAML `distribute.blocks_per_process` (default 1); the pool serves more than one block.

**Guarantee / limits.** A map; no convergence order. An $x_1$ anchor wait fails after five minutes.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch01-mesh-tests; `test_mesh_executor.<b>` (bitwise), `test_mesh_multi_block.<b>`, `test_mesh_exchange_python`.
:::

Local symbols: $n_b$ is the number of local blocks of a rank, $n_p$ the number of ranks and $n_{\mathrm{cell}}$ the
interior cells of a block. $a_{kj}$ is the contribution of cell $j$ to block term $b_k$ of a closure moment.
$\delta_{\mathrm{mach}} = 2^{-53}$ is the unit round-off in double precision.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

`MeshOptionsImpl::from_yaml` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) reads the block options;
the block count is the layout's option `distribute.blocks_per_process`, default 1 ({{< code src/options/layout.yaml >}}).
`MeshImpl::reset` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::reset >}}) requires it positive, gives the Mesh a new identity
for the same-process exchange (@sec-ch13-ghost), clones the block options once per local block and repartitions each
clone's coordinates through its layout, and builds one stage executor that all the blocks use. The worker pool `BlockWorkerPool` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::BlockWorkerPool >}}) runs one
thread per block. On a CUDA device it creates one stream of its own per block (`OwnedStream`). It records the caller's stream in an
event every worker waits on, and records a done event per worker that the caller's stream waits on. The blocks'
kernels thus run on their own streams. `MeshImpl::max_time_step`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::max_time_step >}}) takes the minimum of the local bounds, then one MIN over the
process group, then the Courant factor and the redo halving. `MeshImpl::forward`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}) first lets the blocks agree on how they run (Mesh-agree,
@sec-ch13-agree), refuses a strict block that cannot capture, defers each block's chemistry and aligns their captures
(@sec-ch13-cuts). It runs every block's stage schedule through the pool. With the axial-momentum closure on, it sums
the closure moments of the local blocks, reduces them once over the process group, applies each block's increment and
refills its physical boundaries (@sec-ch07-axial). On the last stage it runs each block's chemistry step, one block
after another, and refills the physical boundaries. It then exchanges the ghosts of every block. `MeshImpl::check_redo`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}}) combines the blocks' local flags on the device (one
device-to-host read when they share a device) before the one reduction
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::decide_retry >}}). Stream assignment is an execution policy, not
evidence of numerical equivalence between decompositions.

@fig-ch01-mesh-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}

#| fig-alt: "Sequence: agree and align; per-block workers run the stages; global phase: closure, chemistry; exchange."
#| echo: false

make_fig()
```

**Why the mesh reduces once.** Three facts of the code, with the round-off of the one sum bounded in step 3.

1. The time step is the minimum of the local bounds, then one MIN over the process group
   ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::max_time_step >}}); a minimum selects an operand and adds no round-off.
2. The redo decision combines the blocks' flags on the device and crosses the process group once
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::decide_retry >}}); a flag is 0 or 1, so the combination is exact.
3. The axial-momentum closure sums each block's closure moments over the $n_b$ local blocks, then once over the $n_p$
   ranks ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}). Each block term $b_k$ is itself a sum of
   $n_{\mathrm{cell}}$ cell contributions $a_{kj}$ (@sec-ch07-axial). A sum of $n$ doubles accumulated in sequence
   has an error of at most $(n-1)\,\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}$ times the sum of the terms' magnitudes. The per-block
   sums therefore contribute at most $(n_{\mathrm{cell}}-1)\,\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}\sum_{k,j}|a_{kj}|$, and the
   combination of the $n_b n_p$ block terms at most $(n_b n_p - 1)\,\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}\sum_k|b_k|$. A different
   block count therefore changes the common increment by round-off only.

: Implementation anchors for the mesh. {#tbl-ch01-mesh-code}

1. Read the options and build the clones and the executor: `from_yaml`
   ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}), `reset` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::reset >}}).
2. Run the blocks' stages through the pool and reduce once: `forward` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}),
   `max_time_step` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::max_time_step >}}),
   `check_redo` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}}).
3. Message tags and the $x_1$ anchor wait: `send_to_block` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::send_to_block >}}),
   `take_x1_anchor` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::take_x1_anchor >}}).

**How to use it.** The `distribute`[^rg-8f3010cdaece] block names the layout and the local block count:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `layout`[^rg-b7bb60acd6d2], `nb1`[^rg-55fe49bed3ce], `nb2`[^rg-cbf2d5a13e1b], `nb3`[^rg-a3366ec76446].
```yaml
distribute:
  layout: slab          # or cubed, cubed-sphere
  nb1: 1
  nb2: 2
  nb3: 1
  blocks_per_process: 2 # local blocks; default 1
```

Refused: a key other than `layout`, `nb1`, `nb2`, `nb3`, `verbose`, `blocks_per_process` and `backend`, and a
non-positive `blocks_per_process`; `backend` is accepted and ignored, the environment `BACKEND` wins
(@sec-ch12-layout). The mesh order of a stage is these lines of `MeshImpl::forward`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}), with the global phase elided:

```cpp
  executor_->agree(vars);
  for (int i = 0; i < static_cast<int>(blocks.size()); ++i)
    executor_->check_strict(i, vars[i], stage);
  if (stage == 0)
    for (auto& b : blocks) b->step_dt = dt;

  for (auto& b : blocks) b->defer_chemistry = true;
  // B3: a segment one block must (re)capture is captured by all of them (its
  // exchanges meet at the same-process rendezvous)
  executor_->align_captures(vars, dt, stage);
  run_block_jobs(
      [&](size_t i) { executor_->run_stage(i, vars[i], dt, stage); });
// ... the global phase: the axial closure over the blocks; on the last stage, each block's chemistry ...
  run_block_jobs([&](size_t i) { blocks[i]->exchange_ghost_zones(vars[i]); });
```

`agree`, `check_strict` and `align_captures` decide, for all the blocks together, whether the stages capture
(@sec-ch13-agree, @sec-ch13-cuts); the deferral line moves the chemistry step out of each block's schedule into the
global phase; the two `run_block_jobs` calls are steps 2 and 3 of the walk-through. A one-block Mesh runs its job on
the caller's thread ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::run_block_jobs >}}).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_mesh_executor.cpp` (`test_mesh_executor.<b>`) | two blocks stepped by `Mesh::forward` through the shared executor equal the pre-executor sequence (each block's local stage, then the exchange); a bare block and a clone own their executors | bitwise (`torch::equal`) | the executor changes who runs the stage, not what runs |
| `test_mesh_multi_block.<b>` (two ranks) | the ghost strips of local and remote neighbours hold the neighbour's value, and both kinds were seen | `allclose` defaults | library defaults |
| `test_mesh_exchange_python` | after a scalar exchange on four blocks, each ghost strip holds its neighbour's rank | exact equality | an integer rank field is copied |

: Source assertions for the mesh. {#tbl-ch01-mesh-tests}

The assertions are {{< code tests/test_mesh_multi_block.cpp Mesh.multi_block_exchange >}} with
`side_is_uniform` ({{< code tests/test_mesh_multi_block.cpp side_is_uniform >}}), and the top-level `assert`
of {{< code tests/test_mesh_exchange.py >}}.

At the pin all three passed on both builds; `test_mesh_executor.release` ran 4 of its 8 cases on CPU (the CUDA
cases skip there) and all 8 on CUDA, and `test_mesh_multi_block.release` ran on two ranks.[^ch01-mesh-ctest] No report
check exists for this section.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A driver-split source applied after a mesh call makes the exchanged ghosts stale before the next advance; this
follows from the call order and is not a measured drift. Remote message tags allow at most 16 blocks per
process. The local $x_1$ anchor wait needs a producer that runs concurrently or earlier and fails after its
five-minute timeout.
:::
